A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PSHuman. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on THuman2.1 and CAPE, ablations, timing measurements, qualitative comparisons, and a 20-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds face-specific quantitative evaluation, additional comparisons, and robustness and failure examples.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same body-face diffusion, noise blending, SMPL-X conditioning, explicit remeshing, and appearance fusion. v2 supplies additional implementation explanations and equations, but does not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Training datasets and quantitative benchmark coverage remain unchanged. However, v2 substantially broadens qualitative coverage with anime/hand-drawn characters, object-occluded inputs, strong lighting and shading, and targeted child/elderly pose-estimation cases in supplementary Figures 13–19. Self-occluded human reconstruction was already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds HiLo to both settings of Table 1 and the geometry comparison, and adds SiTH to Table 1's ground-truth-SMPL-X setting. SMPLX-D joins the carving comparison, and Sapiens-2B appears in the new face-normal comparison. These are limited extensions of the retained comparator suite.

E3.justification: v2 introduces head-specific evaluation using SMPL-X head vertices and KD-tree cropping, plus a separate control removing noise blending. Existing training budgets, benchmark sample totals, appearance viewpoints, and pose-noise settings are retained. Exact split identifiers and the template-free configuration clarify existing experiments rather than establish changed settings.

E4.justification: v2 independently ablates noise blending and quantitatively evaluates facial reconstruction, extends the carving comparison with SMPLX-D, and adds failure, occlusion, lighting, pose-estimation, and stylized-input analyses. The original full-body quantitative ablation and two/four/six-view study are retained and relocated, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate and qualitative reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports face Chamfer distances of 0.423 for PSHuman, 0.524 without the local branch, and 0.447 without noise blending. Additional baseline entries and qualitative robustness, normal-estimation, and failure findings substantially expand the results. Matched original geometry, appearance, pose-noise, timing, user-study, and full-body-ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The diffusion factorization, approximation rationale, and remeshing objective are retained. v2's additional alignment and color-fusion equations express optimization already described in v1; they introduce no substantive new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: photorealistic single-image reconstruction through cross-scale diffusion, SMPL-X guidance, and efficient explicit carving, with strong geometry and appearance results. The revised title and emphasis on direct multiview generation do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 extends the pose-error limitation with incorrect novel-view generation and inconsistent hair/hand details, illustrated in Figure 10. It attributes no-blending artifacts to global/local inconsistency, anime generalization to pretrained diffusion, and lighting robustness to HDR augmentation. These refine the existing mechanism and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds text prompts, background removal and resizing instructions, input-front-view reuse, exact test-scan identifiers, sphere initialization for the template-free setting, and HDR-lighting disclosure. Most training details are relocated unchanged. However, v1's 0.05 CLIP-conditioning dropout rate and PyMAF-X hand-estimation detail are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including HiLo, Sapiens, DeepSDF, rembg, and image-quality metrics, while removing the CFG, PyMAF-X, and Feng et al. references. The introduction more explicitly positions direct multiview generation against front/back-view approaches; the broader related-work framework remains stable.

P1.justification: The title, author list, and selected introduction and method passages are revised. Training details and the comprehensive ablation move into the main text, while supplementary material is regrouped. Most prose and the main introduction–related work–method–experiments–conclusion structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout throughout, combines v1's pipeline and diffusion-block figures into Figure 3, reorganizes comparison panels and tables, and adds face evaluation, carving progression, failure, and robustness displays. Existing supplementary galleries and analyses are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evidence for the facial-reconstruction contribution through head-specific metrics and an isolated noise-blending ablation, clarifies Table 1's template-free setting, and documents concrete failure conditions. These improve validation and transparency. The gains are limited by unspecified sample coverage for the new face evaluation and omission of v1's conditioning-dropout and hand-estimation details; the established method and benchmark results remain unchanged.
